new_tasks.title: Reconcile 0.15 source provenance and publish a verified implementation inventory
new_tasks.deliverable: Audit current Git refs and any explicitly supplied 0.15 snapshot, map exact commits to release requirements, and distinguish implemented, partial, absent and unqualified behavior. Do not rebuild a duplicate feature or treat conversational claims as recovered code.
acceptance: Record source/archive hashes, provenance and relevant changed paths; absent earlier snapshots are explicitly absent, not silently relabeled 0.14.
For every requirement, link the existing implementation issue and identify a runnable test or a concrete missing-test task.
Preserve current main and CI fixes; propose focused recovery PRs to the appropriate owning area instead of mixing product edits into this audit.
Inventory includes document designer lifecycle, two apps/two instances, app-only HTML downloads, real Git auth, GPU fallbacks and numerical/network operations.
Provide exact commands, environments, last verified commits, failing logs and remaining blockers; no artifact link without a real asset and integrity check.

new_tasks.title: Enforce fair numeric-worker and memory budgets across concurrent app sessions
new_tasks.deliverable: Implement the cross-app resource-admission layer for the existing numeric pool. Consume A19 session IDs and A00 cancellation/lifetime contracts; retain A10 ownership of pool scheduling. This is the multi-app slice of adaptive scheduling, not a second worker pool.
acceptance: Two apps and two instances share an explicit browser-wide worker and queued-byte budget, while managed heaps and inputs remain isolated.
Fair dispatch prevents a large/background job from starving small foreground tasks; nested submissions cannot multiply worker counts beyond the budget.
Cancel, dispose or crash one app without terminating other apps; reject stale completions and release transferred/shared-buffer ownership once.
Retain scalar/SIMD threshold selection and report actual workers, copied/shared bytes, allocations and per-app quotas.
Benchmark cold/warm, p95/p99 UI latency and throughput for one versus four apps with identical inputs; retain raw data including regressions.
A19 owns session lifecycle, A11 owns managed scheduling, A12 owns network quotas and A06 owns GC. Changes to shared registries/runtime dispatch require an A00 handoff, not edits from this task.

new_tasks.title: Ship JS and Wasm-SIMD app-publish profiles without blocking on the future Rust port
new_tasks.deliverable: Deliver the 0.15 subset of backend-selectable application publishing using the existing JavaScript managed runtime and optional Wasm SIMD numeric backend. Keep the broader parent open for Rust/Wasm runtime publishing; do not remove its Rust dependency or call numeric Wasm a Rust runtime.
acceptance: Publish selected console, library-entry and WinUI projects with dependency closure and runtime-only assets; downloaded output does not boot the IDE.
Embed nested numeric-worker and SIMD assets, validate safe HTML/script escaping and produce deterministic bytes plus checksums.
Run the downloaded HTML offline and over supported HTTP/HTTPS origins; test missing SIMD, missing WebGPU and absent cross-origin isolation as separate cases.
Reject unsupported native APIs, absent entry points and unavailable backends before download; report supported profiles explicitly.
No repository token, development credential, recovery buffer or implicit network/storage grant is included.
Rust execution remains tracked by SF-A27 and the parent issue; this child can close only with JS/SIMD-specific evidence, never by closing the broader parent.

new_tasks.title: Qualify the 0.15 Git-to-designer-to-multi-app-to-downloaded-HTML release scenario
new_tasks.deliverable: Own only the cross-area acceptance fixture and release evidence. Exercise merged area implementations together; implementation defects return to their existing owner issues. The wider full-parity product-acceptance parent remains open.
acceptance: Open a remote multi-project solution, edit two compatible C# documents in Design/Split/Code, and preserve dirty buffers, undo, keymaps, caret and breakpoints.
Start two project apps and two instances of one app; debug/hot-reload/design-attach one while others keep working; stop/restart must not cross-route output, grants or late callbacks.
Run numeric jobs and real HTTP/WebSocket requests concurrently; test fairness, cancellation and permission revocation without cross-app effects.
Exercise WinUI drawing on supported WebGPU hardware and each fallback separately, with device-loss captures and adapter/backend records; unavailable hardware is explicitly unqualified.
Publish both projects concurrently, verify filenames, checksums and dependency closure, then start the actual downloaded HTML files offline and served without Studio globals.

Exercise private-repository PAT and supported browser OAuth/device flows on a controlled provider account, including cancellation, logout and non-fast-forward rejection; never store secrets in evidence or generated apps.
Keyboard/DPI/light/dark regression includes the supplied Designer button alignment defect and per-document designer switching.
Extract the exact release source archive, rebuild artifacts/packages and examples, compare hashes, and publish remaining incompatibilities and every failed/unsupported platform.
A passing mock, IDE standalone test or fixture simulator is not accepted as an app-export, native SDK, provider-auth or physical-GPU pass.

project_policy.native_parents: retain area hierarchy; release membership is cross-project, not reparenting
views: Release: group by SF Area, filter SF Release=0.15
Agents: group by Agent; show Status, Branch, Lease expires, File locks
Blocked: use native dependencies and explicit task evidence
Epics: native sub-issue progress; do not count parents as leaf throughput
